pharm: Benzimidazole that binds parasite beta-tubulin, inhibiting microtubule assembly and selectively impairing glucose uptake, depleting glycogen and ATP in susceptible intestinal helminths; acts largely locally within the gut lumen due to low systemic absorption.
quick: 500 mg as a single dose (one chewable tablet) for ascariasis/trichuriasis
May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal increases absorption
Avoid in first trimester; weigh benefit later; animal embryotoxicity
Limited data; minimal systemic absorption; generally considered compatible
No adjustment (poorly absorbed, minimal renal excretion)
Use caution; metabolized hepatically; monitor with prolonged/high-dose use
Avoid heavy use (hepatic risk with prolonged therapy)
CBC and LFTs only with high-dose or prolonged therapy
summary: Mebendazole is a benzimidazole anthelmintic indicated for patients one year and older with gastrointestinal infections caused by Ascaris lumbricoides (roundworm) and Trichuris trichiura (whipworm). It is given as a single 500 mg chewable tablet, acts mainly within the gut lumen, and is generally very well tolerated at the standard single dose.
indications: Treatment of patients one year of age and older with gastrointestinal infection caused by Ascaris lumbricoides (roundworm)
Treatment of patients one year of age and older with gastrointestinal infection caused by Trichuris trichiura (whipworm)

dosage.d: 500 mg (one chewable tablet) as a single dose
dosage.n: Chew completely before swallowing; do not swallow whole

dosage.t: If not cured 3 weeks after first treatment

admin: Chew the 500 mg tablet completely before swallowing; do not swallow whole
For patients who cannot chew, place tablet in 2-3 mL water on a spoon; it softens within 2 minutes and can then be swallowed
May be taken without regard to food; a high-fat meal increases bioavailability
No fasting or purgation is required
Treat household and close contacts when appropriate for soil-transmitted helminths
moa: Mebendazole is a benzimidazole anthelmintic. It binds selectively to parasite beta-tubulin, inhibiting polymerization of microtubules and disrupting glucose uptake by intestinal helminths. This depletes the parasite's glycogen stores and ATP, leading to immobilization and death of the worm. Because most of an oral dose remains within the gastrointestinal tract, the drug exerts its effect largely locally.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to mebendazole or any component of the formulation
relative: Children under 1 year (risk of convulsions reported)
Concomitant use with metronidazole (serious skin reactions)
monitor: Complete blood count with high-dose or prolonged therapy
Liver function tests with high-dose or prolonged therapy

preg: Avoid in the first trimester. Published literature has not shown a clear association with major birth defects, but animal studies showed skeletal/soft-tissue malformations, decreased pup weight and embryolethality at doses as low as ~0.2-fold the maximum recommended human dose. Untreated helminth infection also poses risk; weigh benefit versus risk, preferably deferring elective treatment beyond the first trimester.
lact: Limited data; mebendazole is poorly absorbed systemically and only small amounts are expected in breast milk. It is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against maternal clinical need.
renal: No dosage adjustment needed. Mebendazole is poorly absorbed and undergoes minimal renal excretion.
hepatic: Use with caution; mebendazole is metabolized in the liver. Elevated transaminases and hepatitis have been reported mainly with high doses or prolonged courses. Monitor liver function in these settings.

major: Metronidazole (avoid concomitant use; Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis reported)
moderate: Cimetidine (may increase mebendazole plasma concentrations with prolonged therapy)
Carbamazepine and other enzyme inducers (may lower mebendazole levels)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal increases bioavailability.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid heavy alcohol use with prolonged or high-dose therapy due to additive hepatic risk.

rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis (with metronidazole)

monitoring: CBC during high-dose or prolonged therapy
Liver function tests during high-dose or prolonged therapy
Stool examination 3 weeks after treatment to confirm cure
Watch for skin reactions if metronidazole co-administered
counsel: Chew the tablet completely; do not swallow whole
May be taken with or without food
Practice good hand hygiene and wash fruits/vegetables to prevent reinfection
Treat the whole household if recommended
Stop and seek care for rash, blistering, fever, or sore throat
A second dose may be needed if symptoms persist after 3 weeks
pk: Local anthelmintic effect within the gut over days
Plasma Tmax ~4 hours (higher Cmax when taken with a high-fat meal)
Single-dose therapy; clearance of worms over days
Store below 30 C; keep tightly closed; discard unused tablets 1 month after opening
pearls: Single 500 mg chewable dose treats ascariasis and trichuriasis in patients >=1 year
Poorly absorbed and acts mainly in the gut lumen, so it is very well tolerated at standard dosing
Avoid combining with metronidazole due to reports of Stevens-Johnson syndrome / TEN
Marrow suppression and hepatitis are concerns only with high-dose, prolonged regimens (e.g., echinococcosis off-label use)
missed: For single-dose therapy a missed dose simply means taking it when remembered. If a repeat dose was scheduled, take it as soon as remembered; do not double up.
overdose: No specific antidote. Gastrointestinal symptoms may occur; with very high or prolonged doses, alopecia, reversible transaminase elevation, hepatitis, agranulocytosis, neutropenia and glomerulonephritis have been reported. Provide symptomatic and supportive care and monitor blood counts and liver function.
